title: Animating an exported node field makes the node "appear" orphaned
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1], v4.6.stable.mono.official [89cea1439] ### System information Godot v4.6.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8142) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 63.61 GiB memory ### Issue description If I use an animation track to set the value of an exported node type field, the node appears orphaned when accessed from the field. ``` [Export] Node myNode; // An animation track sets the value of this field to another node in the scene public void Check() { // The same animation track calls this method 1 second later GD.Print(myNode == null); // This prints false, the variable is defined GD.Print(myNode.IsInsideTree()); // This prints false, the node appears orphaned } ``` Setting the field's value manually in the editor by dragging in a node, or setting the value via code does not have this issue. Debugging shows the actual node is not orphaned, regardless of how the field value was set. Debugging also showed the instance id to be different between the actual node and the field that was set by an animation. Looking at the raw animation in the scene, it's storing the the node as an serialized object? ``` tracks/1/type = "value" tracks/1/imported = false tracks/1/enabled = true tracks/1/path = NodePath(".:animatedNodeField") tracks/1/interp = 1 tracks/1/loop_wrap = true tracks/1/keys = { "times": PackedFloat32Array(0, 1), "transitions": PackedFloat32Array(1, 1), "update": 1, "values": [null, Object(Node2D,"_import_path":NodePath(""),"unique_name_in_owner":false,"process_mode":0,"process_priority":0,"process_physics_priority":0,"process_thread_group":0,"physics_interpolation_mode":0,"auto_translate_mode":0,"editor_description":"","visible":true,"modulate":Color(1, 1, 1, 1),"self_modulate":Color(1, 1, 1, 1),"show_behind_parent":false,"top_level":false,"clip_children":0,"light_mask":1,"visibility_layer":1,"z_index":0,"z_as_relative":true,"y_sort_enabled":false,"texture_filter":0,"texture_repeat":0,"material":null,"use_parent_material":false,"position":Vector2(0, 0),"rotation":0.0,"scale":Vector2(1, 1),"skew":0.0,"script":ExtResource("2_pyidc")) ] } ``` Which seemed weird since setting the exported field manually just stores the node path. ``` [node name="Root" type="Node2D" unique_id=1227262708 node_paths=PackedStringArray("animatedNodeField")] script = ExtResource("1_pyidc") animatedNodeField = NodePath("Foo") ``` My amateur guess is the animation is setting the object properties instead of making the field reference the intended node. ### Steps to reproduce The included project has two scenes, `root.tscn` reproduces the issue in C#, and a simpler GDScript version in `root-gd.tscn`. Run the scenes and the results are printed to the output. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [animated-export-field-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25150923/animated-export-field-bug.zip)
